items.name: Multiversion concurrency control
items.explanation: A database keeps several versions of each value, and every reader sees a snapshot as of one moment. Readers then do not block writers.

assumedBy.quote: Each serialized etcd request must run through etcd’s boltdb-backed MVCC storage engine, which usually takes tens of microseconds to finish.

items.name: Linearizable and serializable reads
items.explanation: A linearizable read returns the most recent write, which costs a round of agreement with the cluster. A serializable read is answered by one member from what it has, so it is cheaper and can be slightly stale.

assumedBy.quote: Linearizable read requests go through a quorum of cluster members for consensus to fetch the most recent data.

items.name: TLA+ and formal verification
items.explanation: TLA+ is a language for writing down how a system should behave so a tool can check it against every possible ordering of events. It finds bugs that tests rarely hit.

assumedBy.quote: The safety properties of the Liveness Fabric are formally verified in TLA+, and the verification model is publicly available on GitHub.
